title: One research task, three parallel workers and one reassignment

events.label: The research task arrives
events.detail: "Research three open-source vector stores for performance and licensing, and produce a selection report." — a single agent's context cannot hold this much retrieval output; time to split.

events.label: Task reaches the orchestrator
events.detail: The orchestrator is itself a model call: its output is not the answer but the decomposition of the task.

events.label: The split decision
events.detail: Split logic: three subtasks are mutually independent, each with its own tooling needs — retrieval, benchmarks, case history. Dependent subtasks would be chained serially.

events.label: Dispatch A: public-material retrieval
events.detail: Worker A carries its own search tools and its own loop — context isolation is a feature: each worker's window holds only its own task.

events.label: Dispatch B: benchmarks
events.detail: Worker B runs write/query benchmarks with its benchmarking tool.

events.label: Dispatch C: internal cases
events.detail: Worker C collects the company's past selection records — three tasks now in flight in parallel.

events.label: Three tracks running
events.detail: Isolation is also a risk: workers cannot see the whole picture, and stitching their outputs is the orchestrator's job.

events.label: A completes
events.detail: License and ecosystem comparison for the three stores, with source links.

events.label: C completes
events.detail: Two historical selection cases with the reasons each alternative was rejected.

events.label: B fails
events.detail: The benchmark tool timed out 3 times in a row (an old friend from T03); B returns a failure report instead of inventing data — honest failure is repairable failure.

events.label: Failure handling and reassignment
events.detail: Decision: do not re-dispatch B (time budget); instead extend A to fetch the vendors' official published benchmarks — 'who answers for the final result': the orchestrator.

events.label: Second subtask dispatched
events.detail: A's context already holds the first batch, so the marginal cost of the follow-up is lower than spinning up a new worker — reassignment is a scheduling decision too.

events.label: Follow-up completes
events.detail: Official benchmark data for all three vendors arrives; B's gap is closed.

events.label: The synthesis call
events.detail: All three deliverables enter the orchestrator's context and one call drafts the report — context quality at synthesis time decides report quality.

events.label: Report delivered
events.detail: The report carries its evidence chain plus a note that B's subtask was downgraded. When is multi-agent justified: context blowup, specialized division, parallel speed — single agent first, multi-agent later is the evolution discipline.
